page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-64 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor, utilizing simultaneous multithreading with two threads per core. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local NVMe SSD storage or integrated GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC processor delivers top-tier single-core performance, scoring 3433.17 in stress-ng and achieving top 10% rankings in PassMark CPU tests, including physics simulations and extended instruction execution. Multi-core performance is also strong, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 109753.45. The memory subsystem demonstrates robust throughput, recording a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 6539.2 GB/sec and uncached large block read and write speeds of 203.88 GB/sec and 127.63 GB/sec respectively.

The instance is highly capable for compute-heavy workloads such as data compression, database operations, and small-to-medium scale language model inference. It achieves 105.66 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and processes 196.81 tokens per second for prompt processing on 7B LLM models. However, the 2.0 GB per vCPU memory ratio represents a tradeoff, making it less suitable for memory-intensive datasets or applications requiring massive local storage, as no local storage is bundled.
